What country is this in? I'm used to traffic being separated by a double yellow when it is traveling in opposite directions. This is separated by dashed white lines, which usually indicates two lanes traveling the same direction.

America, and maybe a few other countries also. Passing lane has a dashed line. A single dashed line means both sides can pass when safe. A double line with dashes on one side means only one side can pass. A single or double line means no passing.

In America, out of the 8 states I've driven, all have used yellow lines to separate opposing traffic, whether solid, double solid, dashed, or some mix of these. I've never seen white paint separating traffic headed in opposite directions.

Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and white lines are used to separate traffic moving in the same direction, and on the shoulders of paved roads. On one-directional roads, a yellow line appears on the left shoulder, and a white line on the right shoulder. Passing rules are denoted by dashed lines as in the United States.

Source - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_surface_marking#The_Americas
